channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Criminal – Lack of prosecution
item.description: Where a criminal complaint charging a defendant with possession of heroin with intent to distribute and possession of omeprazole was dismissed for lack of prosecution because the commonwealth “refused a court order to bring the alleged drugs in” for a hearing on a motion to suppress, the judge abused his discretion both by deeming the commonwealth’s conduct a failure to prosecute and by refusing the prosecutor's request for a continuance.

item.title: Prisons – Appellate entry fee – Waiver
item.description: Where (1) a Superior Court judge denied a plaintiff’s motion for extra fees and costs to hire an expert witness, (2) the plaintiff sought interlocutory relief from a single justice of the Appeals Court pursuant to G.L.c. 231, §118, and (3) the plaintiff moved for a waiver of the appellate entry fee, the single justice’s order requiring the payment of a partial entry fee must be reversed because the single justice erroneously relied upon G.L.c. 261, §29.

item.title: Search and seizure – Consent – Exit order
item.description: Where a defendant who was ordered out of his vehicle during a routine traffic stop filed a motion to suppress, that motion should have been allowed because (1) the exit order was unlawful and (2) the commonwealth has failed to carry its burden of demonstrating that the defendant's consent was sufficiently attenuated from the unlawful exit order to purge the taint of the constitutional violation.

item.title: DIA wrongfully denied insurer reimbursement claim
item.description: Appeals Court rules Workers’ Compensation Trust Fund must reimburse insurer’s COLA payments, limiting denial grounds under G.L.c. 152 §65.

item.title: AG tells budget writers she needs more lawyers to fight Trump
item.description: Massachusetts AG Andrea Campbell seeks $2.7 million more to hire lawyers for ongoing legal battles against the Trump administration threatening state funds.

item.title: DiZoglio launches reelection amid legislative audit fight
item.description: Massachusetts State Auditor Diana DiZoglio announces her 2026 reelection campaign while continuing her fight to audit the state Legislature despite opposition.

item.title: Retirement – Accidental death – Car accident
item.description: Where the Contributory Retirement Appeal Board denied a plaintiff’s request for accidental death benefits pursuant to G.L.c. 32, §9, the plaintiff’s motion for judgment on the pleadings should be allowed because the undisputed facts establish, as a matter of law, that his mother was engaged in the performance of her work duties at the time of her death in a car accident.

item.title: Zoning – Marijuana – Malden bylaw
item.description: Where a plaintiff has challenged the validity of Malden’s marijuana zoning bylaw, a judgment should enter declaring that the bylaw is unreasonably impracticable and in violation of G.L.c. 94G, §3(a) and §3(a)(2)(ii).

item.title: Attorneys – Expert witness – Waiver of privilege
item.description: Where the plaintiffs in an accounting malpractice action have disclosed their former counsel as an expert witness, they have waived the attorney-client privilege and work product protection related to (1) the attorney’s expert opinions, (2) prior statements he made related to or inconsistent with those expert opinions and (3) the work he performed, documents he reviewed or communications he had related to, or in order to form, his opinions.

item.title: Licenses and permits – Wagering – Preemption
item.description: Where the commonwealth has alleged the operation of a sports betting platform in Massachusetts without a license, the commonwealth’s request for a preliminary injunction should be allowed despite the defendant’s argument that the Massachusetts sports wagering law (G.L.c. 23N) is preempted by federal law.
